messages:
jamie: Observed a weird tail-case on staging: a prefix got handed off, we revoked the guardian lease, but a subsequent read returned stale data (pre-handoff). Logs show revocation ack, then a read serviced from the new owner, but it still returned old KV for ~30s. :thinking_face:

natalie: Ugh. Can you paste the minimal logs and the prefix id?

jamie: prefix=tenant:1234:conv, logs:
```
[2789990000.001] guardian: revoke req -> ownerA
[2789990000.010] ownerA: revoke ack
[2789990000.012] ownerB: claim prefix
[2789990020.200] reader: get(prefix) -> value=v1 (stale)
[2789990030.500] reconciler: detected tombstone/wipe, corrected value -> v2
```
We're seeing a 20s window where reads on ownerB still see v1.

rahul: Hypothesis: revocation ack reached control plane but not ownerB's local cache invalidation, or ownerB applied a snapshot that didn't include last mutation. Two failure modes: (1) revoke lost or reordered relative to KV apply, (2) snapshot/compaction left stale pages.

tess: Another angle: guardian lease has a grace_period (default 15s). If the new owner starts serving before the old owner garbage-collects its KV cache, and there's race between revoke and prefix prefetch/caching, you can read from a local cache that hasn't been invalidated. Did we run with grace_period override?

jamie: grace_period was set to 10s in the failing run. But note the read was 20s after revoke ack. So seems longer than grace.

rahul: Could be double-apply fallback: ownerB serves from its local prefix cache until it detects mismatch and then pulls the authoritative snapshot. If the detection depends on a periodic checksum, that could explain the delay.

natalie: Can we make the revoke path include a monotonic revocation_epoch stored in prefix metadata and push that in the snapshot header? New owner would refuse to serve any cached pages with epoch < current. That would be fast and deterministic.

tess: We already store prefix.version but it's optional and not checked for cache pages. Making it mandatory means a small on-path check when serving: compare page.epoch vs prefix.metadata.epoch. If mismatch, fetch snapshot. Cost: one extra metadata read per cache-miss or per-page serve. Benefit: immediate consistency after handoff.

rahul: Alternative: piggyback invalidation on our sequencer: when revoke occurs, sequencer issues an invalidation event to ownerB via the routing fabric. But that's extra infra and brittle in partitions. I prefer an owner-local defensive check.

jamie: What about combining epochs + short lease extension on revoke? Flow: old owner on revoke asks for short extend to finish GC; new owner won't serve cached pages with older epoch. That gives window for graceful tear-down.

natalie: I sketched a minimal change: store prefix.revocation_epoch (u64) that increments each handoff. On revocation, control plane sets new epoch and includes it in claim response. ownerB sets its local prefix. When serving, check cached_page.epoch >= prefix.revocation_epoch, else fetch authoritative. Pseudocode:
```
claim_prefix(prefix_id, new_owner) {
  prefix.revocation_epoch += 1
  persist(prefix)
  return prefix
}
serve_page(prefix, page) {
  if (page.epoch < prefix.revocation_epoch) {
    fetch_snapshot(prefix)
  } else {
    serve_from_cache(page)
  }
}
```
No synchronous invalidation messages needed.

rahul: That looks good and idempotent. Edgecases: what if old owner had higher epoch but lost its update? Or we observe split-brain where two owners claim increment concurrently? Needs CAS on prefix metadata. Use central store with compare-and-set on epoch to avoid concurrent increments.

tess: Also consider compaction: if compaction rewrites pages it should stamp them with current epoch. Otherwise a compaction rewrite could resurrect an older epoch page. So compaction job must read prefix.metadata and write page.epoch = prefix.revocation_epoch.

jamie: Good call. We also need to handle historical snapshots used for backups or replication — they must carry the epoch so downstream replicas don't accept stale pages.

infra-bot: Monitoring alert created: "prefix.revocation_epoch_delta" > 0 on >15s. Link: https://monitoring/redwood/alerts/1234 :+1:

natalie: Quick perf thought: we should avoid checking epoch on every token-level read. Do it on page load or cache lookup only. Cache index stores page.epoch, so a single compare per page. That's cheap.

rahul: Tests we should add: unit for concurrent claim (CAS), integration simulating packet loss during revoke ack, compaction stamp tests, and chaos test: interleave revoke + snapshot apply + read heavy workload.

tess: Owner tasks: jamie to prototype prefix.revocation_epoch and stamp compaction; rahul to add CAS logic in control-plane claim path; natalie to add integration tests + monitoring; I'll drive rollout plan (canary with small tenants).

jamie: Plan: prototype in a branch, run chaos-kv scenario for 24h, if stable, ship to staging canary 5% traffic, watch prefix.revocation_epoch_delta and stale-read metrics.

natalie: Ack. I'll spin up the test harness and add the test matrix.

rahul: One more nit: keep epoch as 128-bit if we include a node-id prefix to prevent wrap or collisions in weird clock jumps. But u64 CAS should be fine for now.

tess: Sounds good. If we hit anything unexpected, reopen thread. Thanks all. :raised_hands:
